text:
anya: quick question — ran into a warmup race when we hotpatch a new safetensors shard while in-flight requests are streaming off the old one. thoughts on a transactional demux approach?
kevin: curious, can you sketch the failure mode?
anya: sure. flow is: serving runtime has shard A mapped, we start streaming a patch that replaces parts of A (A') while prefix cache + kv cache still reference offsets from old layout. if we switch over mid-stream some requests hit missing offsets => OOM / corrupt reads.
maria: hmm. is this about complete file swap vs per-chunk overlay?
anya: yes. currently we either swap whole file atomically (coarse) or do in-place overlay writes (risky). proposal: introduce a small "demux transaction" primitive so writers publish a new shard as a set of immutable chunk-files and then commit a single light-weight manifest update that atomically swaps routing. readers follow manifest version id.
pranay: sounds promising. that would let streaming readers finish on old chunk set while new requests get routed to new chunk set. how do we handle partial commits & garbage?
kevin: think of it like git refs + CAS objects for chunks. writer uploads chunks -> compute chunk checksums -> upload a commit object listing chunk ids + sizes + root checksum -> an atomic pointer update (manifest version bump). we garbage collect old roots after refcount drops to 0.
anya: exactly. this avoids dual-format boils and gives us a clear rollback path. also helps for mixed-format transitions (safetensors -> safetensors+quant).
maria: what about on-disk layout? mmap-friendly vs file-per-chunk. file-per-chunk makes GC and CAS easier but hurts openfd budgets and random seeks. any perf numbers?
pranay: we benchmarked similar patterns for activation pages: per-chunk with 64KB chunk size had slight head-of-line latency but better tail and easier async eviction. suggestion: chunk size tuned per model layer/weight shape.
kevin: loader interface idea: Loader::begin_demux_write(shard_key) -> DemuxWriter(handle). write_chunk(id, bytes) -> commit(version_meta). commit returns version_id. runtime switch uses compare_and_swap(manifest_ptr, old, new). code sketch: 
```
let tx = loader.begin_demux_write("gpt-7b/layer_12");
tx.write_chunk("c0", buf0);
tx.write_chunk("c1", buf1);
let v = tx.commit({ root_checksum: "sha256:...", chunk_table: [..] });
manifest.cas(old_version, v);
```
maria: need checksums on each chunk and overall root so readers verify in-flight. also require loader to expose alignments so mmap readers can still use zero-copy paths by aggregating contiguous chunk ranges into mmaps.
pranay: also add a reader-level compatibility mode: read_version(version_id) returns a Table of (chunk_id -> ReaderHandle). ReaderHandle hides whether it's mmaped, file-backed or streamed. that keeps runtime code simple.
anya: fallback plan: if compare_and_swap fails, writer should abort and GC its unreferenced chunks. if readers encounter a missing chunk id they should fall back to the contiguous legacy path (mmap whole file) to keep latency bounded.
kevin: we should add a small v2 header flag in safetensors metadata: "demux_enabled": true, plus optional chunk_hint table. migrating older artifacts sets flag false. loader will accept both.
pranay: test matrix: concurrent read/writes, partial commit (crash after some chunks uploaded), eviction under mem pressure, mmap openfd exhaustion, quantized chunk migration. we should add fuzz tests for mismatched chunk tables.
maria: perf counters to add: chunk-open rates, failed CAS count, reader-fallback rate, average chunk size, manifest switch latency. these help tune chunk size and GC thresholds.
anya: decision proposal: prototype demux in loader-shim as opt-in flag, keep default behavior unchanged. aim to land RFC follow-up with API surface + GC semantics. owners: kevin (API sketch + prototype), pranay (bench + fuzz tests), maria (reader abstraction + perf counters). timeline: prototype in 2 weeks, RFC doc by end of sprint.
kevin: one more note — we should avoid coupling to storage backend semantics. chunk CAS should be storage-agnostic (S3 puts + etag or local FS with inode+ctime). manifest CAS is logical (put manifest with version and then update pointer in a separate metadata store).
pranay: agree. also add a small compatibility shim: if storage doesn't support atomic pointer update, use a leader elect + linearized manifest appends + checkpoint compaction.
maria: ack. i'll draft reader API with ReaderHandle and edgecase behavior for missing chunks.
anya: thanks all. small win if this prevents the hotpatch OOMs. loader-bot: created ticket INF-5287 "demux transactional warmup prototype" and linked this thread.
kevin: lgtm
pranay: lgtm
anya: cool, moving to prototype.
